findings.statement: Reported gross margin percentage fell by three basis points; excluding gasoline price inflation it rose 10 basis points, which is not a noticeable widening of the markup.
findings.rationale: The filing states a small reported decrease and a modest increase only after excluding gasoline price inflation, so neither reading shows a noticeable widening of the overall markup.

quotes.text: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points. Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points.

findings.statement: Gross margin in core merchandise categories, as a percentage of their own sales, increased 15 basis points, across all categories.
findings.rationale: This is the closest measure of merchandise markup and it rose, but 15 basis points is small and the filing does not call it a notable widening; the same filing shows ancillary businesses fell.

quotes.text: The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points. The increase was across all categories.

findings.statement: Management describes a pricing philosophy that does not seek to maximize prices charged in the short term.
findings.rationale: Qualitative statement of strategy that makes a deliberate large markup widening less likely, though it does not describe this year's result.

quotes.text: We do not focus in the short-term on maximizing prices charged, but instead seek to maintain what we believe is a perception among our members of our “pricing authority” – consistently providing the most competitive values.

response.rationale: The filing shows total gross margin percentage slightly down for the year and up only modestly excluding gasoline, with core merchandise margin up 15 basis points. The evidence does not support a noticeably wider markup; it points to a roughly stable one.
